Comments: E-Services Gateway lists vehicle licensing as one of its services. No evidence of driver licensing data integration with a central data exchange hub beyond the e-gateway portal.

revision_notes: The Road Transport (Amendment) Act 2023 (Act 14 of 2023) legally establishes a Register of Driving Licences and a Register of Merit Points, requiring courts to notify the Licensing Authority of traffic-offence convictions so points/suspensions can be applied - a genuine, if largely manual, data-sharing mechanism; a digital driving licence also now exists via the SeyID app / monServis portal (since 2023). Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: Seychelles has national identity database infrastructure, and the e-Services Gateway provides some passport/immigration-related services. No specific evidence of passport/immigration data integration with a central exchange platform. DICT handles government IT but agency systems operate in silos.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The Seychelles Electronic Border System (SEBS), launched November 2022 by the Ministry of Internal Affairs with DICT, digitises embarkation/disembarkation and API/PNR data and feeds it in real time into DICT-managed immigration databases, drawing on biometric passport data (introduced November 2022). This is an operational, automated data feed into a government-held immigration data store, beyond 'Planned', so upgraded to 'Partially integrated' (4); there is no evidence it is yet interoperable with the wider e-Services Gateway or other exchange functions, so not 'Fully integrated'.

revision_notes: SRC's ePayment facility (launched June 2024) is directly integrated with the ASYCUDA customs data system, and a Tax Management System under development since 2023 is designed to share a single payroll dataset automatically between SRC and the Seychelles Pension Fund. This is real, documented integration for specific tax/customs data flows, so upgraded from 'Planned' to 'Partially integrated' (4), though not yet comprehensive across all tax types.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Data Protection Act 2023 (enacted December 19, 2023) replaced the 2003 Act. Designates the Information Commission as data protection authority. Includes provisions for cross-border data transfer, data subjects' rights, DPO appointment, and breach notification. Access to Information Act also provides a legislative basis. Seychelles is the first African country to recognize the CBPR mechanism in its law.

revision_notes: Confirmed via the Official Gazette text of the Data Protection Act 2023 (Act 24 of 2023, in force 22 December 2023) and the Information Commission's own site: the Act establishes the Information Commission as data protection authority with investigation, enforcement-notice and sanctioning powers, and governs cross-border data flows (s.47). This is a genuine primary legal instrument for data governance; Value Code 3 ('Yes') confirmed, no change.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Data Protection Act 2023 restricts personal data transfers outside Seychelles unless comparable protection exists. Seychelles is the first African country to recognize the CBPR mechanism. The Act mandates data protection by design, DPO appointments, and creates the Information Commission as enforcement authority. However, no specific data localization mandate for all government data. Enforcement capacity of the Information Commission is not fully documented.
